$comment: A POLICY DOCUMENT, not a deployed role. Deployment (Phase 18) has not started — there is no AWS account, no CDK stack, and nothing here has ever been applied. This file is what infra/ (CDK v2, per CLAUDE.md's repo layout) is expected to synthesize when that phase runs, and what this phase's tests audit against instead of a live role. Resource ARNs use a wildcard account/region segment (':*:*:') because no account exists yet to fill them in; the table name segment is exact and is cross-checked against packages/ledger/src/tables.ts's TABLE_LOGICAL_NAMES by packages/ledger/test/iam-advisory.test.ts, along with a table prefix of 'chaperone' (packages/config's DDB_TABLE_PREFIX default) so a rename of either drifts loudly instead of silently.

roles.name: chaperone-gateway-task-role
roles.description: The ECS Fargate task role for the gateway process itself (docker/gateway.Dockerfile, infra's future Fargate service). This is the identity that runs gate.ts, approve.ts, and api.ts, and — until an isolated advisory worker exists (see the bedrock role below) — packages/advisory/src/localRunner.ts's putAdvisory/setQuarantineAdvisoryScore calls also execute under this role, not a separate Bedrock-scoped one. CLAUDE.md's append-only rule is enforced here at the table-statement level, not just in packages/ledger's client code: the ledger-event statement grants PutItem and read verbs only — no UpdateItem, no DeleteItem, no BatchWriteItem — so a bug in application code cannot become a write IAM would have allowed anyway.

roles.name: chaperone-bedrock-advisory-role
roles.description: The scoped role for an isolated advisory-scoring worker — the deployment target this table of permissions is designed for, even though packages/advisory/src/localRunner.ts does not yet run as a separate worker (see the gateway role above for what actually executes today; splitting the two is tracked as deployment work, not done in this phase). This is 'the Bedrock role' this phase's tests mean: it may call Bedrock, and it may read a quarantine row to build the prompt for it, and it may do nothing else. No statement here names ledger-event or pin at all, and the one statement that names quarantine grants only GetItem/Query. There is no PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, or BatchWriteItem anywhere in this role — a compromised or misbehaving model call cannot alter the record a resident is being asked to trust, cannot touch the append-only ledger, and cannot re-pin anything.
